newsitem.title: MEXICO: Leading opponent won't run for Mexico City mayor.
newsitem.headline: Leading opponent won't run for Mexico City mayor.

text.p: The opposition politician who polls say has the best chance of winning next July's Mexico City mayor's election ruled himself out of the running on Friday.

Diego Fernandez de Cevallos, of the conservative National Action Party (PAN), said in a radio interview he had definitely decided not to run for mayor of the capital in the first election to be held for the post next year.
"I have decided not to. I have made my position clear ... definitely not," he said.
The mayor's job has, since the 1910-17 Mexican Revolution, been held by a member of the long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) chosen directly by the President of the Republic.
But, as part of President Ernesto Zedillo's commitment to opening up Mexico's closed political system, the mayor will be chosen in a free election next year.

A poll published this week in Reforma newspaper showed Fernandez de Cevallos as the potential candidate with the highest ratings and best name recognition. He had a 39 percent approval rating, against less than 20 percent for most of the 17 names suggested from different parties.

None of Mexico's three big parties has yet officially chosen its candidate. Likely names being suggested for the ruling PRI's candidate include the current mayor Oscar Espinosa Villareal and Senate leader Fernando Ortiz Arana.
The left-wing PRD may field its former leader Porfirio Munoz Ledo or ex-presidential candidate Cuauhtemoc Cardenas.
Fernandez de Cevallos said he favoured ex-party leader Carlos Castillo Peraza or PAN politician Francisco Paoli as the PAN's candidate.
